papers.title: Chemical abundance patterns at z=1-7: Carbon, Nitrogen, Neon, Sulphur, and Argon abundances from JWST spectroscopy
papers.authors: E. Cataldi, F. Belfiore, M. Curti, B. Moreschini, A. Marconi, F. Mannucci, G. Cresci, A. Feltre, M. Ginolfi, A. Amiri, M. Arnaboldi, S. Bhattacharya, E. Bertola, C. Bracci, M. Ceci, A. Chakraborty, Q. D'Amato, C. Kobayashi, C. Marconcini, R. Maiolino, L. Querci, M. Scialpi, L. Ulivi, G. Venturi, M. V. Zanchettin
papers.abstract: The relative abundances of chemical elements in the interstellar medium (ISM) trace the history of star formation and chemical enrichment in galaxies. We investigate the abundance patterns of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), neon (Ne), sulfur (S), and argon (Ar) in star-forming galaxies at z=1-7, combining ultra-deep JWST/NIRSpec observations from the MARTA survey with archival spectroscopy. We assemble 244 galaxies with [OIII]4363 detections and derive direct Te-based abundances. New empirical strong-line calibrations for N/O, Ne/O, S/O, and Ar/O extend the analysis to an additional 514 galaxies. We find distinct abundance-metallicity trends. N/O is enhanced by 0.18 dex in median relative to local galaxies, with a stronger enhancement at low metallicity. Direct measurements reveal decreasing S/O and Ar/O with increasing metallicity, while strong-line measurements suggest a flattening at higher metallicities, especially for S/O. We also identify a stellar-mass dependence in the O/Ar-Ar/H plane, with lower-mass galaxies exhibiting lower O/Ar at fixed Ar/H, consistent with differences in star-formation efficiency and delayed SNe Ia enrichment. Ne/O remains approximately constant up to 12+log(O/H)=8.2, with a mild increase at higher metallicities and no significant redshift evolution. C/O tentatively increases with metallicity, broadly following the local relation. Finally, a forward model shows that observational selection affects the abundance ratios differently: it mainly restricts the accessible metallicity range for Ne/O and Ar/O, but preferentially selects galaxies with enhanced N/O at low metallicity, with a weaker effect for S/O. These results provide new constraints on chemical enrichment at high redshift and highlight the importance of accounting for selection effects when interpreting abundance-metallicity trends.

papers.title: The Balmer Absorber Strength Problem of Little Red Dots
papers.authors: Hanpu Liu, Eliot Quataert, Bingjie Wang, Jenny E. Greene, Yan-Fei Jiang
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) commonly show Balmer absorption features. Some observed LRD spectra have weaker absorption in H$\alpha$ than in H$\beta$, in apparent contradiction to atomic physics according to standard attenuation models. This tension is naturally resolved when one considers emission from the absorbing medium itself, which is ignored in the standard model: when the Balmer absorption is optically thick, a non-negligible source function could fill in the H$\alpha$ absorption trough and reduce its observed absorption equivalent width (EW). With proof-of-concept photoionization models we show that the source function of H$\alpha$ could be systematically stronger than that of H$\beta$. This is due to radiative trapping preferentially populating the $n=3$ level of neutral hydrogen, which operates efficiently when the medium is optically thick to H$\alpha$ but not very optically thick to Paschen-$\alpha$. Such line-dependent source functions could lead to significant corrections to the expected EW and selectively weaken H$\alpha$ absorption, consistent with observations. Quantitatively, this depends on the distance of the absorbing medium and its internal structure, providing a new diagnostic of the environment around LRDs. Future modeling of the absorbers may also potentially open a new avenue for estimating the mass of the central engine.

papers.title: Arepo-CD: Coupling Collisional $N$-Body Dynamics with Moving-Mesh Magnetohydrodynamics
papers.authors: Chuizheng Kong, Hui Li, Long Wang, Yunwei Deng, Elizabeth Moreno-Hilario
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM)
papers.abstract: Star formation is a hierarchical, clustered process in turbulent giant molecular clouds (GMCs), where close stellar encounters can strongly affect cluster evolution and feedback. However, gravitational softening in many hydrodynamic simulations of GMCs limits the treatment of these encounters. We present Arepo-CD (Collisional Dynamics), a framework that couples star-by-star collisional $N$-body dynamics to the moving-mesh magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code Arepo. Star-star interactions use unsoftened gravity, while interactions involving gas or collisionless components remain softened. Compact stellar subsystems are identified on the fly and evolved with a fourth-order forward symplectic integrator and slow-down algorithmic regularization coupled to the native Arepo timestep hierarchy. Benchmark tests against the collisional $N$-body code PeTar show good agreement in cluster core collapse and subsequent expansion, radial density profiles, and stellar velocity distributions. Coupled to the Rigel star formation and feedback model, Arepo-CD follows cluster formation and early evolution in radiation MHD simulations of a $10^5~M_\odot$ turbulent molecular cloud. In the fiducial GMC comparison, the collisional and softened-gravity runs yield similar star formation histories and integrated star formation efficiencies. Nevertheless, close gravitational encounters during the embedded phase generate a substantial runaway population, with a velocity tail extending beyond 100 km/s. Ejected massive stars redistribute radiative feedback into the surrounding lower-density medium and produce a more extended distribution of heated gas. Arepo-CD provides a practical and computationally efficient framework for studying collisional stellar dynamics and its coupling to gas evolution and feedback during star cluster formation in realistic galactic environments.

papers.title: Discovery of a Broad-Line Active Galactic Nucleus at $z = 9.98$
papers.authors: Xingyao Cai, Akio K. Inoue, Masafusa Onoue, Suzuka Arai, Yoshinobu Fudamoto, Rohan P. Naidu, Pascal A. Oesch, Jenny E. Greene, Ivo Labbe, Jorryt Matthee, Anna de Graaff, Yuma Sugahara, Ken Mawatari, Pratika Dayal, Xi Kang
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has uncovered a previously unexplored population of faint active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in the early Universe. We present MoM-BL-z10 at $z=9.9837\pm0.0009$, identified through a systematic search for broad-line AGNs at $z\geq6$ using public JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra from the DAWN JWST Archive. The PRISM spectrum exhibits a broad component in H$\beta$ at 5.35 microns. A narrow+broad Gaussian fit yields a broad H$\beta$ detection at S/N = 3.87, with FWHM = $3480^{+2040}_{-950}$ km s$^{-1}$ and $L_{{\rm H}\beta,{\rm broad}}=1.25^{+0.33}_{-0.31}\times10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$. The detection of [Ne III] $\lambda3870$ and the high [Ne III]/[O II] and [O III]/H$\beta$ ratios further support the AGN interpretation. Its rest-frame UV and optical continuum slopes, compact NIRCam morphology, and a tentative MIRI F770W detection suggest similarities to Little Red Dots (LRDs). The broad H$\beta$ detection enables the first virial SMBH mass estimate at $z\sim10$. We derive $M_{\rm BH}=3.6^{+5.8}_{-1.7}\times10^7 M_\odot$ and $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=0.11^{+0.10}_{-0.07}$ using the standard single-epoch virial calibration and quasar bolometric correction. We also consider an alternative scenario adopting the LRD-specific bolometric correction and assuming $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=1$, which yields $M_{\rm BH}=2.1^{+0.6}_{-0.5}\times10^6 M_\odot$. Under either scenario, the inferred SMBH mass at a cosmic age of only 470 Myr highlights the challenge of rapid BH growth in the early Universe, suggesting super-Eddington accretion from a stellar-mass seed or a more massive seed. As the highest-redshift broad-line AGN identified to date, MoM-BL-z10 provides a new observational benchmark for understanding the early growth of supermassive black holes.

papers.title: A combined HST and JWST analysis of the stellar population in Draco II
papers.authors: Axelle C. Raffin, Giacomo Cordoni, Helmut Jerjen, Gary S. Da Costa, Maria V. Legnardi, Anna F. Marino, Antonino P. Milone, Fabrizio Muratore
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Solar and Stellar Astrophysics (astro-ph.SR)
papers.abstract: Draco II (Dra II) is one of the faintest and most metal-poor Milky Way satellites known, yet its nature as either an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy or an extended globular cluster remains debated. We perform a photometric analysis of the stellar population of Dra II reducing deep multi-band observations from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). We select Dra II member stars based on their proper motions and photometric quality criteria. For the first time, optical and infrared photometry are combined to produce a stellar catalogue reaching 50 percent completeness at $F814W = 26.5$ mag (corresponding to the absolute magnitude $M_{F814W} = 10.1$ mag). The colour-magnitude diagram confirms that Dra II hosts an old stellar population with an age of $13.5_{-1.5}^{+1.7}$ Gyr at a distance of $19.2\pm0.9$ kpc. We measure an $\alpha$-enhanced stellar population with a low mean metallicity of $[\rm Fe/H]_{CaHK} = -2.38 \pm 0.17$ dex and confirm the presence of an intrinsic metallicity spread of $\sigma_{[\rm Fe/H]} = 0.85 \pm 0.13$ dex. We identify 10 unresolved main-sequence binary stars in the HST catalogue with mass ratios $q > 0.5$ in the mass range $0.43<M_1/M_\odot<0.71$, corresponding to a binary fraction of $f_{bin}^{q>0.5} = 0.21 \pm 0.07$. This value is higher than those typically observed in globular clusters and lies near the upper range measured in open clusters. The stellar mass function is best modelled by a single power law with a slope of $1.53\pm0.26$ over the mass range $0.13$--$0.77\ M_\odot$. We find no evidence of mass segregation. Consistent results are obtained independently from the JWST catalogue. Combining these findings strongly suggests that Draco II is best classified as an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy rather than a globular cluster.

papers.title: Unveiling the correlation between the UV 2175 Å dust attenuation bump, PAH emission, and gas-phase metallicity at cosmic noon
papers.authors: L. Arriscado, I. Shivaei, L. A. Boogaard, A. Mizener, D. Calzetti, P. G. Pérez-González, F. Rodríguez Montero, G. H. Rieke, Y. Zhu, A. Battisti, A. J. Bunker, E. Curtis-Lake, T. Díaz-Santos, Z. Ji, P. Rinaldi, B. Rodríguez del Pino, S. Tacchella, A. Varo-O'Ferrall, C. C. Williams, J. Witstok
papers.abstract: The UV 2175 Å attenuation bump is one of the most prominent yet poorly understood features of galaxy attenuation curves. Its main candidate carrier is polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) molecules, which are more prevalent in high-metallicity environments. We present the first systematic study of the relationship between PAH abundance and the UV bump in 49 galaxies at cosmic noon (1.5 < z < 2.7), examining its dependence on stellar mass, star formation rate (SFR), and V-band optical depth. For 19 galaxies, we also investigate gas-phase metallicity using oxygen abundances. We measure the bump amplitude from VLT/MUSE spectroscopy and derive galaxy properties, including the PAH-to-dust mass fraction $q_{\rm PAH}$, through spectral energy distribution fitting with Prospector, combining JWST/NIRCam and JWST/MIRI photometry. Oxygen abundances are derived from strong-line diagnostics using Keck/MOSFIRE and JWST/NIRSpec data. We find a positive correlation between bump amplitude $E_{\rm bump}$ and $q_{\rm PAH}$ (Spearman $\rho = 0.60$). UV bumps are rarely detected at low $q_{\rm PAH}$, supporting PAHs as their primary carriers. Both $E_{\rm bump}$ and $q_{\rm PAH}$ correlate with stellar mass, oxygen abundance, and optical depth, and anticorrelate with specific SFR, suggesting that PAHs and the UV bump are suppressed in low-metallicity, dust-poor, and/or intensely star-forming environments. This is consistent with PAH destruction in environments with limited dust shielding and/or strong radiation fields. A principal component analysis of $E_{\rm bump}$, $q_{\rm PAH}$, optical depth, specific SFR, and oxygen abundance explains 97% of the variance, suggesting that previously reported correlations with stellar mass reflect an underlying dependence on metallicity. Finally, variations in dust geometry may explain the wide range of bump amplitudes (0-0.5 mag) at high $q_{\rm PAH}$.

papers.title: Ammonia Fitting of Multiple Velocity Components in High-Mass Star-Forming Regions
papers.authors: T. Withers, S. Sadavoy, M. Chen, J. Di Francesco, R. Friesen, J. Keown, E. Rosolowsky, H. Kirk, A. Ginsburg, L. D. Anderson, P. Caselli, D. Elia, E. Figura, H.-L. Liu, A. P. Marston, F. Motte, S. Offner, S. Pezzuto, P. Sanhueza, E. Schisano, N. Schneider, I. W. Stephens
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Solar and Stellar Astrophysics (astro-ph.SR)
papers.abstract: We perform a multiple velocity component analysis of ammonia (NH$_3$) gas from KEYSTONE, a Green Bank Telescope survey covering 11 giant molecular clouds (GMCs) at distances from 0.7 to 2.7 kpc. We extend existing codes to enable simultaneous fitting of up to three velocity components in NH$_3$ (1,1) with radiative transfer. Using our multiple component fitting technique, we produce the best maps of the centroid velocity and velocity dispersion in these clouds to date. Over the entire survey, multiple velocity components were seen in 13% of pixels where we detect and fit NH$_3$ emission, primarily in clusters at the heart of the GMCs. In these multiple component pixels, the median measured NH$_3$ linewidth decreased by a factor of 1.4 compared to equivalent single-component measurements, but there are also significant cloud-to-cloud variations. Regions with multiple velocity components tend to be found in the densest zones of the GMCs and at the sites of high-mass star formation, indicative of multiple filaments, cores, or complex velocities associated with the formation of massive stars. Disentangling these velocity features will allow future quantitative analysis of coherent motions, such as infall and outflow, in these complex environments. The multi-component data products are available on the CADC.

papers.title: Link between the properties of circumgalactic outflows and the recent star formation history of their host galaxies
papers.authors: Ismael Pessa, Lutz Wisotzki, Constanza Muñoz López, Tanya Urrutia, Ramona Augustin, Thierry Contini, Yucheng Guo, Daria Kozlova, Haruka Kusakabe, Sowgat Muzahid, John Pharo
papers.abstract: Galactic outflows play a key role in galaxy evolution, yet their connection to the star formation history of their host galaxies remains poorly constrained. Building on previous work modeling extended Mg II emission of galaxies observed with VLT/MUSE to infer outflow properties, we investigate how these properties depend on the recent SFH. We derive non-parametric SFHs by fitting spectroscopic and photometric data with linear combinations of single stellar population models, and compute star formation rates over different timescales sensitive to recent stochastic bursts. We find moderate correlations between these SFRs (and sSFRs) and the kinematic properties of the outflows, namely maximum velocity and radial acceleration rate. Such correlations are not recovered using SFR tracers based on [O II] luminosity or parametric SFHs, highlighting the importance of capturing bursty star formation on timescales consistent with the traveling time of ejected gas into the circumgalactic medium. Using the extent and kinematics of the Mg II halos, we estimate each galaxy's outflow launching time and compute the SFR averaged over the relevant timescale. We identify a correlation between this SFR and the maximum outflow velocity, although it is not significantly stronger than those obtained using fixed averaging timescales. This suggests that the properties of Mg II halos are shaped by a series of star formation events rather than by a single dominant burst. Lastly, we find faster outflows in galaxies whose recent star formation is dominated by one or a few concentrated episodes, whereas galaxies with star formation spread more evenly over time exhibit slower outflows. These results indicate that the circumgalactic medium acts as a dynamical archive of recent star formation, linking bursty galaxy growth to outflow kinematics and providing a direct observational constraint on feedback models.

papers.title: The MIni-Halos in MIni-Clusters (MIMIC) project: New insights into the origin of mini-halos from a LOFAR, uGMRT, and MeerKAT study of diffuse radio emission in Abell 496 and ZwCl 235
papers.authors: F. Ubertosi, S. Giacintucci, A. Botteon, A. Bonafede, T. Pasini, M. Balboni, N. Biava, G. Brunetti, T. Clarke, V. Cuciti, F. de Gasperin, P. Domínguez-Fernández, H. Edler, F. Gastaldello, M. Gitti, K. Kolokythas, G. V. Pignataro, C. J. Riseley, R. J. van Weeren, T. Venturi, J. Zuhone
papers.abstract: We aim at investigating the presence of diffuse radio emission in low-mass (M$_{500}\leq3\times10^{14}$ M$_{\odot}$), relaxed galaxy clusters. We present a pilot study for the MIMIC (MIni-halos in MIni-Clusters) project, focusing on Abell 496 and ZwCl 235, using LOFAR (54, 144 MHz), uGMRT (400, 650 MHz), and MeerKAT (1.28 GHz) data, as well as Chandra X-ray data. We detect diffuse radio emission in the central 100 kpc of both Abell 496 and ZwCl 235, spatially confined within sloshing-induced cold fronts seen in X-ray images. The diffuse sources satisfy the classification criteria for radio mini-halos and represent the least powerful known to date, with 1.4 GHz radio powers of $(2.2\pm0.2)\times10^{22}$ W/Hz in Abell 496 and $(1.3\pm0.3)\times10^{22}$ W/Hz in ZwCl 235. The mini-halos have steep spectra ($-1.9\leq\alpha\leq-1.4$), and in Abell 496 we find outward steepening of the spectral index. In both clusters, the radio and X-ray surface brightness are correlated over the diffuse source extent, with sub-linear or nearly linear slopes depending on frequency. Separately, we present the properties of two extended (>200 kpc) tailed radio galaxies in both clusters. The steep spectra, sub-linear radio-X-ray correlations, and confinement within cold fronts suggest that contribution from fossil plasma advected from the central radio galaxy and plausible turbulent re-acceleration are at play in Abell 496 and ZwCl 235. These two systems allow us to extend mini-halo scaling relations toward the low-power regime. We confirm a strong correlation between the mini-halo radio power and the cool core X-ray luminosity, with $P_{1.4} \propto L_{X,70}^{1.5\pm0.2}$. We find, for the first time, tentative indications that mini-halos with steeper radio spectra may preferentially be associated with lower core X-ray luminosities and lower radio power. (abridged)

papers.title: PIANISTpy: A JAX-based Python package for velocity-anisotropic astrophysical equilibrium models
papers.authors: Barry T. Chiang, Frank C. van den Bosch, Hsi-Yu Schive
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO); Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM); High Energy Physics - Phenomenology (hep-ph)
papers.abstract: The hierarchical assembly of dark matter haloes and galaxies via mergers and anisotropic mass accretion naturally imprints non-trivial velocity anisotropy onto haloes and galaxies, an empirical fact emerging from cosmological simulations. However, dynamical studies based on idealised numerical simulations typically assume isotropic velocity distributions for the systems studied. This is mainly because no tools exist to construct anisotropic initial conditions with fully self-consistent (i.e., physical and instability-free) truncation boundary conditions for finite spatial extents. Here we present the first such analytical framework that performs truncation in phase space, with two distinct approaches to guarantee either the monotonicity of output distribution functions or identical truncated density profiles. We additionally present the open-source JAX-based GPU-accelerated Python package PIANISTpy (Particle Initial conditions with ANISoTropy) for constructing spherical, non-rotating initial conditions, supporting arbitrary double-power-law analytical radial density profiles and a library of analytical anisotropy profiles. This framework further permits the construction of systems with non-analytical anisotropy profiles via an arbitrary linear superposition of all implemented analytical anisotropy models as basis functions. PIANISTpy also outputs 3D velocity profiles and line-of-sight-integrated observables with end-to-end differentiability for rapid gradient-based Monte Carlo inference, and self-consistent local dark matter velocity distributions of anisotropic haloes beyond the unphysical Maxwell-Boltzmann simplification adopted in terrestrial detection experiments. We discuss use cases and demonstrate PIANISTpy's orders-of-magnitude higher numerical solver accuracy and superior dynamical stability of particle initial conditions relative to existing tools, including galpy and AGAMA.

papers.title: KROME-X: a GPU-ready library for chemistry and microphysics in astrophysical simulations
papers.authors: Alessandro Lupi, Tommaso Grassi, Stefano Bovino
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM)
papers.abstract: KROME is a Python pre-processor that writes a complete Fortran solver of chemistry and microphysics for each chemical network, widely used in astrophysical simulations. We introduce here KROME-X, a complete rewrite of KROME in modern C++, which incorporates updated physics. A code generator translates a declarative network description into a compact core (rates, right-hand side, analytic Jacobian, thermal terms, and tables), which a fixed, header-only runtime integrates with a C++ port of the `backward differentiation formula' method of CVODE (SUNDIALS). The physics is validated against legacy KROME and independent references. On the legacy test cases KROME-X reproduces legacy KROME to the accuracy of the solvers, wherever the physics is the same, and is up to 13.5 times faster at equal tolerance. On NVIDIA A100 GPUs, it can outperform its share of a computing node from a few thousand cells per call, with the highest throughput (5 to 30) obtained for $10^5$ cells per batch. Networks of hundreds of species still run faster on the CPU due to the GPU's limited memory capacity. The new version also includes, among other changes, on-the-fly co-evolution of a photon field alongside chemistry, which conserves photons exactly; the secondary ionizations using the photoelectron energy of each absorption; dust evolution in size and temperature with a true grain energy equation; line cooling rates rebuilt from current atomic and molecular data, and incorporating optical thickness effects. KROME-X therefore represents the natural successor of KROME and provides a portable, extensible framework for astrochemical kinetics on both CPUs and GPUs for future hydrodynamic simulations.

papers.title: The H IX galaxy survey IV: What does the molecular gas reveal in HI eXtreme galaxies
papers.authors: V. A. Capa, H. Dénes, K. A. Lutz, T. H. Brown
papers.abstract: Galaxies with extreme amounts of neutral atomic hydrogen (HI), known as HI-eXtreme (HIX) galaxies, paradoxically exhibit normal or low star formation rates. To investigate the bottleneck in their star formation, we present ALMA CO(1-0) observations for five HIX survey galaxies: ESO208-G026, ESO378-G003, ESO381-G005, ESO417-G018, and ESO055-G013. While these systems possess massive, extended HI discs, their molecular gas discs are compact with normal H$_{2}$ masses relative to their stellar mass. Dynamical modelling with 3DBarolo reveals that the HI and molecular gas are kinematically consistent. Both gas phases show high velocity dispersions, indicating enhanced turbulence compared to regular late-type galaxies. We calculate the specific angular momentum for the stellar, atomic, and molecular components alongside the global stability parameter ($q$). Most of the system angular momentum is stored in the HI discs, rendering them globally stable against collapse. This stability suppresses the atomic-to-molecular gas conversion, as evidenced by extremely long HI depletion times contrasted with typical H$_{2}$ depletion times. The high angular momentum and HI excess likely originate from past gas accretion or recent tidal interactions; this is especially apparent in ESO378-G003 and ESO381-G005, which exhibit extended HI structures and positive tidal indices.

papers.title: The MAGE Project: Size Evolution and Disk Formation in Massive Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn
papers.authors: Zhiyuan Yao, Avishai Dekel, Romain Teyssier, Rachel Somerville, Nir Mandelker, Zachary Andalman, Ulrich Steinwandel, Zhaozhou Li
papers.abstract: We investigate size evolution and disk formation with a new suite of eleven cosmological zoom-in simulations, Massive Assembly of Galaxies in the Early universe (MAGE), run with RAMSES at $\sim10\,\mathrm{pc}$ resolution until $z\simeq9$. The target galaxies span stellar masses of $M_\star\simeq2\times10^8$-$3\times10^{10}\,M_\odot$ at $z=9$. The stellar half-mass radius grows steeply with stellar mass at low masses, turns over near $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$, and evolves weakly with redshift. The intrinsic UV sizes in MAGE overlap the compact end of observed distributions, including the compact strong-line systems, but not the more extended population at $z>9$. Dust, PSF-limited size measurements, and our overdense environments may contribute to this offset. In the simulations, stars dominate the mass within the half-mass radius above $M_\star\simeq5\times10^8\,M_\odot$, where the central circular speed exceeds a characteristic stellar-feedback scale. Outflows are then increasingly retained within the galaxy, consistent with gas recycling on galactic rather than halo scales, which sustains central gas supply and drives a compaction-like central buildup. The turnover in size at $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$ coincides with rapid growth of rotational support to $v/\sigma\simeq1.5$-$3$ in star-forming gas and stars younger than 10Myr, as the central circular speed exceeds the halo virial speed, which the star-forming gas velocity dispersion tracks. The subsequent low central gas fraction, declining central star formation, and younger outskirts suggest the onset of inside-out quenching.

papers.title: NGC 3227 Blinks: An Extreme Changing-Look Event in a Seyfert Galaxy
papers.authors: Kaiwen Zhang, Michael S. Brotherton, Pu Du, Dong-Wei Bao, Bi-Xuan Zhao, Feng-na Fang, Yan-Rong Li, Chen Hu, Ming Xiao, Keith Horne, Gerard A. Kriss, Daniel Proga, Jian-Min Wang
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; High Energy Astrophysical Phenomena (astro-ph.HE)
papers.abstract: We report a rapid optical changing-look event in the Seyfert galaxy NGC 3227: the optical continuum faded by more than 70% and broad H-beta emission nearly disappeared within weeks, before recovering within two months. Damped random walk simulations calibrated to the source's normal variability show that such a decline is unlikely for stochastic accretion fluctuations (p = 0.002). Simultaneous Swift monitoring reveals X-ray spectral hardening, pointing to enhanced line-of-sight absorption. During the dim state, reverberation mapping yields a persistent 6-8 day lag between the continuum and broad H-beta, showing that the broad-line region continued to reverberate and placing the obscurer interior to the broad-line region. Photoionization calculations require a fully ionized, Compton-thick column with N_H ~ 1.5 x 10^24 cm^-2 to reproduce the optical continuum suppression. Together, these observations demonstrate that compact, high-column-density obscurers interior to the broad-line region can produce extreme optical changing-look behavior on week timescales.

papers.title: Unveiling Accretion-Disk Reverberation Beneath BLR Contamination with TILDE
papers.authors: Sungho Jung, Jong-Hak Woo
papers.abstract: We present a Bayesian framework, Two-stage Inference for Light curve DEcomposition (TILDE), for mapping the accretion disk and the broad line region (BLR) from active galactic nuclei (AGN) multi-band light curves. By inferring delayed BLR contamination from the underlying disk variability, TILDE provides the delay measurements of the disk as well as the BLR. We validate TILDE using synthetic data, finding that TILDE recovers the known time delays of the disk and BLR. By applying TILDE to the Seoul National University AGN Monitoring Project sample, we find that the inferred BLR light curves match the observed H$\beta$ emission light curves, providing consistent BLR lags compared to the reported H$\beta$ lags. Using the lag spectrum, effectively corrected for the BLR contamination, we find that the disk size is broadly consistent with the standard thin-disk model, suggesting that BLR contamination can significantly bias the disk size derived from the cross-correlation analysis of the broad-band photometry. These results demonstrate that the new inference method is a powerful tool for determining both disk and BLR sizes from broad-band photometry in the era of time-domain surveys.

papers.title: B-fields In STar-forming Region Observations (BISTRO): Technical Foundations for Quantitative 450/850 $μ$m JCMT SCUBA-2/POL-2 Polarimetry
papers.authors: Ray S. Furuya, David Berry, Pierre Bastien, Tetsuo Hasegawa, Masafumi Matsumura, Koji Kawabata, Kazunari Iwasaki, Per Friberg, Simon Coudé, Lapo Fanciullo, Thiem Hoang, Yasuo Doi, Hua-bai Li, Jia-Wei Wang, Tao-Chung Ching, Hiroko Shinnaga, Hiroyuki Nakanishi, Sarah Graves, A-Ran Lyo, Junhao Liu, Janik Karoly, Jihye Hwang, Glenn J. White, Doris Arzoumanian, Sarah Sadavoy, Kohji Tomisaka, Pham Ngoc Diep, Mehrnoosh Tahani, Nguyen Bich Ngoc, Archana Soam, Hsi-Wei Yen, Chakali Eswaraiah, Vera Könyves, Jeong-Eun Lee, Valentin J. M. Le Gouellec, Ekta Sharma, Le Ngoc Tram, Frédérick Poidevin, Tie Liu, Mark Rawlings, Najimudeen Bijas, Fumitaka Nakamura, Rachel Friesen, Jean-François Robitaille, Yoshiaki Misugi, Raiga Kashiwagi, Takashi Onaka, Motohide Tamura, Harriet Parsons, Tyler L. Bourke, David Eden, Huei-Ru Vivien Chen, Nagayoshi Ohashi, Jongsoo Kim, Shih-Ping Lai, Keping Qiu, Di Li, Woojin Kwon, Shu-ichiro Inutsuka, Kate Pattle, Derek Ward-Thompson, BISTRO Collaboration
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM)
papers.abstract: We present five technical validations of SCUBA-2/POL-2 polarimetry on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope at 450 and 850 $\mu$m, using 174 archival fields in 69 molecular cloud regions and subsets appropriate to each test. Extended-source calibration avoids a deterministic shift of $\Delta\beta=-1.05$ in the dust emissivity index $\beta$ that would result from calibrating extended emission using peak brightness. We modeled Stokes $I$ noise with additive and signal-dependent components. The measured median ratio of surface-brightness noise at 450/850 $\mu$m is 25. Independent tests of Stokes $Q,U$ noise support approximately equal additive variances and weak error correlations, providing a basis for propagating polarization uncertainties. Corrections determined for individual fields reduce additive zero-level offsets of order $1$ mJy arcsec$^{-2}$ in the 450 $\mu$m Stokes $Q$ and $U$ intensities. The three-step regression leaves a median combined residual amplitude of $0.07$ mJy arcsec$^{-2}$. Independent comparisons with SOFIA/HAWC+ at 154 and 214 $\mu$m support the correction in strongly affected fields. We matched the 450 $\mu$m maps to the modeled 850 $\mu$m beam and the common $12.6''$-$300''$ range of angular scales. We compared three reductions of the same 450 $\mu$m observations across 30 sources. Taking the median angular residual relative to the final product for each source, we find that beam matching reduces the median over sources from $6.3^\circ$ to $4.7^\circ$. After matching, 29 of the 30 sources have median residuals below $10^\circ$. We also quantified how residual $Q/U$ offsets propagate in ratios of polarization fractions, differences in spectral indices, and polarization angles. These validations provide procedures and quantitative references for interpreting POL-2 measurements and combining them with polarimetry at other wavelengths.

papers.abstract: We compared 450 and 850 $\mu$m POL-2 observations from the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope at $12.6''$ resolution. The median absolute difference in polarization angle between bands is $6.7^\circ$ across 21 regions. For total intensity $I\propto\nu^\alpha$ and polarized intensity $PI\propto\nu^\gamma$, 24-27 of 35 regions have $\gamma<\alpha$, allowing for $3\sigma$ limits on weak polarized intensities. The median $\gamma-\alpha$ is $-0.51$, ranging from $-0.57$ to $-0.45$ under these limits. The ratio of polarization fractions is $P_{450}/P_{850}=0.69\pm0.02_{\rm sys}\pm0.03_{\rm stat}$, with no detected dependence on the angle difference. We suggest that the dependence of alignment on grain size offers the simplest explanation of these findings. For optically thin components sharing a polarization angle and opacity law, temperature mixing reproduces the median $-0.51$ only if the warm dust is polarized less efficiently than the cold dust. If the cold dust is at 10 K or warmer and the warm dust at 40 K or cooler, the median requires a ratio of warm to cold effective polarization efficiencies $r\lesssim0.18$. We tested mixtures with opacity index $\beta=2$ in four fields against Herschel dust temperatures and Green Bank Ammonia Survey kinetic temperatures. We assumed equal gas and dust temperatures, ammonia tracing cold gas, and model ranges of 3-20 K for cold dust and 25-40 K for warm dust carrying at most half the mass. Mixtures matching both temperatures cannot reproduce $\gamma-\alpha$ within $1\sigma$ in three fields, including OMC 2 tentatively, even for $r=0$. Allowing warm dust at 10-100 K and up to 95% of the mass permits solutions only for $r\leq0.041$. To explain these three fields by temperature mixing, we need wider model ranges and a very strong contrast in polarization efficiency. The origin of this contrast remains undetermined.

papers.title: Ballistic mixing: stellar mergers drive internal mixing in extremely massive stars, with implications for proto-globular cluster pollution
papers.authors: J. Roman-Garza, C. Charbonnel, A. Rantala, T. Fragos, M. Gieles, L. Ramírez-Galeano
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Solar and Stellar Astrophysics (astro-ph.SR)
papers.abstract: Extremely massive stars, with masses of $10^3$-$10^4$ M$_\odot$, have been proposed as potential sources of the chemical enrichment associated with multiple populations in globular clusters. Early on the main sequence, these stars reach central temperatures of 65 to 75 MK, enabling nucleosynthesis through the CNO, NeNa, and MgAl cycles, producing abundance patterns similar to those observed in the so-called cluster's second population. Stellar mergers are among the leading formation channels for extremely massive stars. In this work, we follow the formation of a $\sim6700$ M$_\odot$ star via 253 stellar mergers, drawn from a direct $N$-body star cluster simulation with properties similar to the densest star clusters observed at redshift $z\sim10$. We evolve each star as a 1D stellar model and construct the merger products from mixing and shock heating prescriptions calibrated to 3D simulations of parabolic collisions. We find that entropy-based mixing efficiently transports nuclear-processed material from the convective core to the envelope, while merger-driven heating promotes chemical homogenization. As a result, the stellar surface becomes enriched with H-burning products, producing abundance patterns consistent with those observed in globular cluster multiple populations and supporting the role of merger-formed extremely massive stars as potential sources of early chemical enrichment in proto-globular cluster-like conditions.

papers.authors: Giacomo Bortolini, Matteo Correnti, Angela Adamo, Michele Cignoni, Monica Tosi, Göran Östlin, Arjan Bik, Daniela Calzetti, John M. Cannon, Flavia Dell'Agli, Bruce G. Elmegreen, Helena Faustino Vieira, Kathryn Grasha, Kelsey E. Johnson, Thomas S.-Y. Lai, Drew Lapeer, Sean T. Linden, Matteo Messa, Alex Pedrini, Julia Roman-Duval, Elena Sabbi, Linda J. Smith
papers.abstract: We present the spatially resolved star formation history (SFH) of the interacting, low-mass, gas-rich galaxy pair NGC 4485/NGC 4490, based on deep JWST/NIRCam imaging obtained as part of the FEAST program. Using resolved stars' near-infrared color-magnitude diagrams (CMDs) and the SFERA 2.0 CMD fitting code, we reconstruct the SFH of the system, including the tidal bridge connecting the two galaxies. We find that recent star formation is widespread across the system, extending beyond the main bodies of the galaxies into the tidal bridge and other off-center areas. In particular, a significant fraction of the recent star formation in NGC 4485 occurs outside its central region. All major regions of the system exhibit two prominent episodes of enhanced star formation, occurring around 0.5-1 Gyr and 10-30 Myr ago, with the tidal bridge showing the largest increase relative to its average star formation rate. These peaks in star formation activity occur a few hundred million years after the epochs of the first and second pericenter passages predicted by independent dynamical models, supporting a scenario in which repeated tidal interactions triggered the observed bursts through gas redistribution and compression. Our results place direct observational constraints on the formation history of NGC 4485/NGC 4490 and provide evidence for the important role of galaxy interactions in driving spatially extended, bursty star formation in low-mass galaxies.

papers.abstract: The Euclid survey provides images with extraordinary potential for studies of the low-surface-brightness Universe, including intracluster light (ICL). However, to realise this promise, the data must be carefully treated to minimise background variations while preserving the signal from diffuse structures. In this work, we describe the post-processing and measurement procedures used for studies of ICL with Euclid. We demonstrate that we are able to substantially reduce background variations without resorting to a small-scale background subtraction. By injecting simulated clusters into the real images, we show that our approach preserves the faint outskirts of extended sources. On scales of several arcminutes, we can reliably detect surface-brightness levels around 27.5 mag arcsec$^{-2}$ in $Y_\textrm{E}$, $J_\textrm{E}$, $H_\textrm{E}$, and 29 mag arcsec$^{-2}$ in $I_\textrm{E}$. As a result, we can obtain accurate measurements of the ICL in individual clusters from the local Universe out to z~0.8 with uncertainties on the order of 10% in surface brightness, 10 degrees in position angle, and 0.1 in ellipticity. Our ability to measure the diffuse light with Euclid is thus set to meet expectations and revolutionise our understanding of the ICL.

papers.abstract: Intracluster light (ICL) offers a luminous route for measuring the shapes and orientations of cluster haloes. We used Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1) images to quantify ICL shapes for 205 clusters at $0.1 \leq z \leq 0.8$ selected from the eROSITA All-Sky Survey and the Dark Energy Survey. We measured the ICL properties across five bands ($I_\mathrm{E}$, $Y_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}$, $H_\mathrm{E}$ and the coadded $YJH_\mathrm{E}$), and find that the shape parameters are consistent across the filters, with the $H_\mathrm{E}$ band probing the profiles to the largest cluster-centric distances ($0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}\sim100$ kpc). The ICL ellipticity ($e=1-b/a$) distribution peaks at 0.5, consistent with halo ellipticities inferred from strong and weak lensing studies, suggesting that the ICL traces the large-scale structure of the clusters. Cluster cores, dominated by brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) light, are round ($e\sim0.2$), while the ICL becomes progressively more elongated at large radii, reaching an ellipticity of $\sim0.5$ by $0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}$. We find that the ICL is closely aligned with the BCG (87% lie within 30$^\circ$), but shows a weaker alignment with the satellite galaxy distribution (61% within 30$^\circ$). Robust position angles could be measured using the ICL for 63% of the sample, whereas position angles could be measured for only 30% of the sample using the satellite galaxies. Stacking clusters in redshift bins allows measurements of the ICL surface brightness to $0.6$-$0.8R_{200\mathrm{c}}$ and ellipticity beyond $0.3$-$0.4R_{200\mathrm{c}}$ (300-400 kpc), but we observed a plateau in the ICL ellipticity beyond $0.1R_{200\mathrm{c}}$. These results demonstrate the capability of Euclid to characterise the ICL morphology with high statistical precision, allowing new constraints on cluster halo structure and its evolution with redshift.

papers.abstract: We present a homogeneous analysis of the intracluster light (ICL) in approximately 300 galaxy clusters spanning $0.2<z<1.5$, combining Sunyaev-Zeldovich-selected clusters from the South Pole Telescope and optically selected clusters from Euclid, and comparing results with Hydrangea simulations. We measured the brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) within elliptical isophotes of semi-major axis 50 kpc, and ICL between 50 and 200 kpc. We show that the Euclid Wide Survey can detect ICL in individual massive clusters ($M_{500} \gtrsim 10^{14.2}\,M_{\odot}$) out to at least $z\sim1.5$, with detection rates of 70-80%. This indicates that diffuse stellar envelopes are common, although not ubiquitous, in massive clusters throughout this redshift range. Using a uniform methodology, we place improved constraints on ICL fraction evolution. ICL contributes about 40% of the combined BCG and ICL light and 20% of the total cluster stellar light, with both fractions remaining approximately constant across $0.2<z<1.5$ at fixed cluster mass. This implies that the relative partitioning of stellar mass between the BCG, ICL, and satellite populations is largely established by $z\sim1.5$. However, the ICL properties of individual clusters may still change as they evolve, since the sample does not represent an evolutionary sequence. This behaviour is consistent with a scenario in which the BCG and ICL are assembled together through the accretion, stripping, and eventual merging of the same population of massive galaxies ($>10^{10}\,M_\odot$). The inferred ICL fraction also depends systematically on wavelength, while remaining largely insensitive to the adopted outer integration radius of 200-600 kpc. These results highlight the importance of homogeneous ICL analyses and constrain the evolution of diffuse stellar components in clusters.

papers.abstract: Colour provides key information to constrain the stellar population of the intracluster light (ICL), the diffuse light within galaxy clusters. We derive radial colour profiles ($Y_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$, $I_\mathrm{E}-H_\mathrm{E}$) of the brightest central galaxy (BCG) and ICL for 168 galaxy clusters from the Dark Energy Survey redMaPPer catalogue within the redshift range $0.1 < z < 0.75$ and halo mass $M_{\rm 200m} > 10^{14.05}M_\odot/h$, within the Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). By stacking the light profiles measured using elliptical annuli on the BCG and ICL images, we reliably measure the ICL colour out to approximately 300 kpc, over which we find a colour gradient, with the ICL becoming bluer than the BCG out to approximately 150 kpc. Using stellar population synthesis (SPS) models, we find that near-infrared (NIR) colours are sensitive to metallicity, but not age. Thus, we measure a metallicity profile in the BCG and ICL that extends out to 300 kpc for a statistical sample for the first time. While the colours, and the detection of a colour and metallicity gradient, are robust, we note that our metallicity measurement is dependent upon our choice of both SPS model and colour. We find that the metallicity of the BCG is super-solar [$\log_{10} (Z/Z_\odot) > 0.1$], while the ICL is metal-poor [$\log_{10}(Z/Z_\odot)\approx -0.5$], placing the first statistical constraint on the metallicity of the ICL out to large radii. These results support our current understanding of BCG and ICL formation: BCGs form predominantly through mergers with massive galaxies or the cores of satellite galaxies, while the ICL grows via the tidal stripping of lower-metallicity stars from the outskirts of massive satellite galaxies.

papers.title: Evaluating Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection for Identifying Unusual Galaxy Morphologies in CEERS and NGDEEP
papers.authors: T. B. Surakan, J. S. Kartaltepe, R. Pattnaik, C. K. Binu, I. G. Cox, T. Y. Hsiao, R. A. Lucas, F. Pacucci, G. Troiani, L. Y. Aaron Yung
papers.abstract: Galaxy morphology out to $z\sim 6$ provides insight into galaxy formation and evolution, but identifying rare or structurally complex systems is difficult due to observational limits and the scale of modern imaging surveys. Here, we apply AdaCLIP, a Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection (ZSAD) model built upon the Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) model and adapted using non-astronomical anomaly-detection datasets, to identify structurally unusual galaxies without galaxy-specific anomaly-detection training or morphological labels. We extract anomaly scores and 768-dimensional feature embeddings from 38,853 galaxies in the Cosmic Evolution Early Release Science (CEERS) and Next Generation Deep Extragalactic Exploratory Public (NGDEEP) surveys, and compare the resulting anomaly scores with parametric GALFIT and nonparametric statmorph measurements. The feature embeddings reveal structure associated with galaxy morphology and observational properties, while anomaly scores show modest trends with structural measures, including asymmetry, concentration, $M_{20}$, and size, but weaker or less consistent trends with Sérsic index, axis ratio, smoothness, and Gini coefficient. These results highlight the potential of ZSAD as a scalable tool for identifying unusual galaxy morphologies in large astronomical imaging surveys, including those anticipated from the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

papers.title: A Little Red Dot emerging from a nitrogen-rich UV-luminous galaxy with Very Massive Stars
papers.authors: Alberto Torralba, Jorryt Matthee, Rui Marques-Chaves, Fabrice Martins, Benjamín Navarrete, Gabriele Pezzulli, Edoardo Iani, Rohan P. Naidu, Gabriel Brammer, Claudia Di Cesare, Anne Hutter, Gauri Kotiwale, Ruari Mackenzie, Sara Mascia, Romain Meyer, Daniel Schaerer
papers.abstract: JWST is revealing abundant populations of high-$z$ galaxies with unforeseen properties: UV-luminous galaxies with high nitrogen enrichment, populations of very massive stars (VMSs; $>100\ M_\odot$), and early forms of massive black hole growth such as the Little Red Dots (LRDs). Here we present all these phenomena appearing simultaneously in COLA1, a luminous ($M_{\rm UV}=-21.3$) galaxy at $z=6.6$. New NIRSpec medium-resolution data reveal a blue UV continuum ($\beta_{\rm UV}=-2.5$) with strong emission lines including NIV] $\lambda1486$, stellar P Cygni profiles, and broad HeII $\lambda1640$. We fit the UV with stellar population models, and find that the models including VMSs (limited to $300\ M_\odot$) are statistically preferred. The best-fit stellar population has $M_*\approx10^8\ M_\odot$, and a young age of $2.4\pm0.8$ Myr. The rest-optical shows a redder continuum ($\beta_{\rm opt}=-1.1$) and broad Balmer lines with Balmer absorption akin to LRD spectra. By evolving the best-fit stellar population we find that the UV could dim by 1-2 mag in $\sim5$ Myr, and hence this system would be observed as a typical V-shaped LRD. We measure a supersolar $\rm log_{10}(N/O)=-0.07\pm0.05$ and subsolar $\rm log_{10}(C/O)=-0.64\pm0.11$; therefore $\rm log_{10}(N/C)=+0.58\pm0.12$. The independent density-sensitive NIV] $\lambda\lambda1483,1486$ and CIII] $\lambda\lambda1906/1909$ ratios require two zones with $n_e\gtrsim10^{6.5}$ cm$^{-3}$ and $n_e\lesssim10^{3.5}$ cm$^{-3}$, respectively. We estimate $\rm log_{10}(N/C)>1.3$ (2$\sigma$) for the dense zone, requiring extreme N/C enrichment mechanisms such as highly rotating $>100\ M_\odot$ VMSs, tidal disruption events, or supermassive stars. We speculate that runaway collisions of massive stars in a dense stellar cluster may have lead to the seeding of an intermediate-mass black hole resulting in the formation of an LRD.

papers.title: The Structural Anatomy of Galaxies: Environmental Dependence of Morphological and Quenching Evolution at 0.1 < z < 0.5
papers.authors: Can Xu, John D. Silverman, Qiusheng Gu, Daniela Galárraga-Espinosa, Andreas L. Faisst, Emanuele Daddi, Hassen M. Yesuf, Angelo George, Esra Bulbul, Zeyu Gao, Lalitwadee Kawinwanichakij, Takumi S. Tanaka, Yunjing Wu, Jialai Wang, Michiru Maruyama
papers.abstract: We investigate how cluster environments affect galaxy star formation, structure, and stellar populations using spectroscopically-confirmed galaxies in X-ray-selected eROSITA clusters, that have deep HSC-SSP imaging and DESI DR1 spectroscopy. At 0.1<z<0.5, we compare dust-corrected Ha star formation rates (SFRs), effective radii (Re), bulge-to-total light ratios (B/T), and Dn4000 between cluster satellites and a stellar-mass- and redshift-matched field control sample. We identify UVJ-quiescent galaxies and divide the UVJ star-forming population at log(sSFR_Ha)= -10.5 yr-1 into actively star-forming and Ha-low systems, the latter referred to as green-valley (GV) galaxies. Cluster--field differences depend strongly on stellar mass, projected cluster-centric radius, and galaxy population. Cluster star-forming galaxies show modest SFR suppression but weak structural offsets. The strongest coupled signatures occur among Ha-low UVJ-star-forming galaxies, particularly low-mass satellites at R<0.5R500, which have lower SFRs, smaller light-weighted sizes, larger B/T, and larger Dn4000 than matched field counterparts. Quiescent galaxies show weaker structural offsets but retain a positive Dn4000 residual. We quantify the joint signal using a Mahalanobis distance based on matched residuals in SFR, Re, B/T, and Dn4000 with a field--field reference covariance. The multivariate offset is largest for low-mass GV galaxies and decreases toward larger projected radius. The broader radial extent of SFR suppression relative to structural offsets suggests that star-formation suppression has a broader environmental reach than structural transformation. These results show that environmental quenching and structural transformation are most strongly coupled in the Ha-low transition population.
